text: You already know this dataset has two real problems: a missing customer name on order 1005, and a negative quantity on order 1014. This lesson fixes both properly, instead of just noticing them.
df.isna gives you a same-shaped grid of True and False; chain .sum on that and you get a count per column. Exactly one missing value in this entire twenty-row dataset — customer_name, on order 1005.

Customer 504 only shows up on that one order, so there's no other row to recover a real name from. fillna replaces the NaN with a clear placeholder, Unknown Customer. dropna would be the wrong call here — it would throw away an otherwise perfectly good row.

Here's the trap: checking duplicated on customer_name flags 7 rows, but that's not 7 real duplicates — it's pandas correctly noticing that customers like Dana Whitfield placed more than one order. Check duplicated on order_id instead, and you get the honest answer: zero accidental duplicates.

A negative quantity isn't a missing value, so isna won't catch it — it needs its own explicit check. The tilde in front of bad_qty flips every True and False, meaning keep everything that is NOT a bad quantity. That takes you from 20 rows down to a clean 19.
With the data actually clean now, next lesson builds new columns on top of it — a real line_total, and logic that a simple arithmetic expression can't express on its own.
